analyzed_vuln.description: The crash is caused by a reachable assertion in decode_R13_R2000: `assert(dat->byte == 0xb)` at line ~322. For malformed/truncated DWG input, the parser state (`dat->byte`) is not guaranteed to be 0xb before entering this routine, but the code uses a hard assert instead of validating and returning an error. This leads to process abort (DoS) rather than graceful parse failure.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In llvmfuzz, inputs beginning with 'AC' are routed to `dwg_decode` (`libredwg/examples/llvmfuzz.c`), which dispatches R13-R2000 files to `decode_R13_R2000`. A crafted short/invalid DWG header (as in the provided PoC) causes `dat->byte` to differ from 0xb at function entry, triggering the assert and aborting. No memory corruption is required; this is an assertion-based denial of service on invalid input.
